chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not wear the mals (flat shoes), for they are the footwear of Pharaoh, and he was the first to adopt the mals.'

key_terms.الْمَلْس: Flat shoes or slippers without heels

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing flat shoes (mals) in Shia jurisprudence and why?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration linking the Prophet of God’s advice to avoid 'al-mals' (flat, heel-less shoes) to the concept of *khuruj* (arrogance), as Pharaoh was the first to adopt this style as a symbol of his supreme authority. Shia scholars often interpret this not merely as a prohibition of a specific shoe type, but as a broader warning against adopting the distinctive dress of the arrogant or tyrannical to signify self-importance. This connects physical adornment with spiritual humility, a key theme in Shia ethics regarding *zuhd* (asceticism) and avoiding *istikbar* (pride).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not wear the flat (shoes) for these are the shoes of Pharaoh<sup>la</sup>, and he<sup>la</sup> was the first one to take to the flat (shoes without heal curve)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather, al-Hassan ibn Rashid who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘Do not use an al-Mals footgear (one without heels and strip between the toes); it is the kind of the footgear of the pharaoh who was the first to use such footgear.’”
